# Fabric decision record

| claim_id | disposition | evidence | condition | confidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A-WARM | supported | BM-A-WARM,BM-B-WARM,BM-D-WARM | Supplied valid warm benchmark series only: A, B, and D each have n=3; this does not cover cold, mixed, censored, or unsupplied workloads. | medium |
| A-COLD | unknown | BM-A-COLD | Supplied cold series for A only: n=3, median 200 ms, with one additional censored run; no cold acceptance threshold is published. | unknown |
| B-ISOLATION | supported-with-bounded-scope | SEC-B-ISOLATION,SEC-A-BIND | Supplied workspace-only mount and scoped-credential configuration only; no claim is made about unsupplied provider, host, availability, or recovery boundaries. | medium |
| B-MIGRATION | unknown | CON-MIGRATION | Immediate direct migration from the legacy fabric to B within the required 14-day window, without using D as a bridge. | low |
| C-THROUGHPUT | rejected | BM-C-POOLED | The only supplied C run pools warm and cold latency samples; workload-mixed latency cannot support one throughput distribution or a universal throughput claim. | high |
| D-MIGRATION | conditional | PROP-D,CON-MIGRATION,CON-ROLLBACK | D is a proposed legacy-compatible bridge and is usable only if a timed rehearsal proves compatibility within 14 days and proves rollback to preserved prior state. | low |
| D-RECOVERY | unknown | INC-D-RECOVERY | Recovery under D; the supplied incident says recovery was delayed and the recovery owner was not assigned. | unknown |
| CON-MIGRATION | required | CON-MIGRATION | Every selected plan must provide a legacy-compatible stage within 14 days. | high |
| CON-OWNER | required | CON-OWNER | Cleanup and recovery owners must be named before cutover. | high |
| CON-ROLLBACK | required | CON-ROLLBACK | Before cutover, a rollback trigger must be testable and the prior state must be preserved. | high |

## Decision summary

Use D as a legacy-compatible migration bridge within 14 days, then cut over to B only after isolation, provider, benchmark, ownership, recovery, and rollback gates pass; retain A solely as a gated workload-specific optimization and reject C's invalid pooled claim. The unresolved boundaries are A cold acceptability, direct-to-B migration feasibility, D recovery ownership, and B provider behavior.
